When the app tries to fit a mathematical curve to your data, it needs an initial guess for the shape of that curve. A poor starting guess can cause the fitting process to produce a bad result. To avoid this, the app automatically tries out many different starting guesses before committing to a final answer. This process is called a grid search. Instead of starting from just one random spot, the app starts at many different spots first, figures out which one seems most promising, and then starts the careful fitting from there. This makes it much more likely you'll find a genuinely good fit. Once the best starting point is identified, the app runs the actual curve-fitting process (called nonlinear least-squares fitting) to fine-tune the result.
